text:
Sam Lee: thinking about the internal API redesign — should we push for gRPC/protobuf across all service-to-service traffic or a gateway-first approach? want pros/cons for runtime, observability, and rollout UX.
Marta Gomez: +1 to weigh ops overhead. gRPC gives typed contracts and smaller payloads but complicates edge clients.
Raj Patel: gRPC is nice for low-latency RPCs between backend services. But we need HTTP/JSON at the edge for 3rd-party integrations and dashboard callbacks.
Alice Zhou: big question: do we force protobufs everywhere and auto-generate gateway JSON translation, or keep mixed paradigms? auto-translation can hide contract mismatches. :thinking:
Sam Lee: what about retries and idempotency semantics? gRPC status codes vs HTTP codes differ and our client SDKs need consistent behavior.
Nate Chen: for retries we should standardize on application-level idempotency keys. transport shouldn't leak into developer UX.
Marta Gomez: observability: tracing automatic with gRPC (binary headers) but JSON adds more noise. Gateway adds hop — need distributed tracing across the gateway.
Raj Patel: telemetry-wise, we need consistent per-route metrics in Console. Gateway can emit normalized metrics so Console dashboards don't care about transport.
Alice Zhou: rollout UX: canarying a proto change vs a JSON shape change — proto is stricter (breaking changes are explicit). With gateway we could accept multiple JSON shapes and translate, allowing smoother rollout.
Sam Lee: proto versioning proposal I sketched: keep enums additive, reserve field IDs, use wrapper messages for experimental fields. snippet: ```proto
message CreateModelRequest {
  string name = 1;
  map<string,string> metadata = 2;
  // experimental fields go in an extension wrapper
  Experimental extras = 100;
}
message Experimental {
  string metadata_v2 = 1;
}
```
Marta Gomez: hmm I worry about the translation layer becoming a huge compatibility surface. who owns the adapters? infra or each platform team?
Raj Patel: infra should own the generic gateway and common adapters. Product teams own model-specific translations. split responsibilities avoids bottlenecks.
Nate Chen: auth propagation: gRPC supports full context propagation but the gateway needs to validate tokens and pass short-lived mTLS to services. adds complexity for Private customers.
Alice Zhou: also quota enforcement — do we do it at gateway (single source) or at service side for more granular limits? gateway gives global quotas, service gives per-model quotas. both probably needed.
Sam Lee: sounds like hybrid is emerging: protobufs + gRPC between core services, gateway for edge + JSON translation, infra-owned adapter patterns, standardized idempotency keys and tracing headers, quotas layered. any glaring downside?
Marta Gomez: added ops burden and testing surface. need contract tests that run in CI against generated JSON<->proto adapters.
Raj Patel: +1. propose a small RFC to define the adapter contract, instrumentation headers, and rollout checklist (compat tests, canary traffic %s, rollback signals).
Nate Chen: canary checklist idea: 1) schema diff; 2) contract-tests pass; 3) gateway translation enabled in shadow mode; 4) gradual traffic 0->5->25->100; 5) monitor latency, error rate, trace spans.
Sam Lee: awesome. I'll draft RFC and include that checklist. tagging @devops-bot to create an issue template for canary runs. :+1:
devops-bot: Created issue #4123: "RFC: internal API adapter + gateway rollout checklist" assigned to Sam Lee. <https://go/redwood/issues/4123>
Alice Zhou: thanks — happy to review the RFC. quick note: include snippet for client SDK behavior (uniform retry semantics + error mapping).
Sam Lee: will do. closing loop — thanks all.
